description: Qualifying surviving spouse age 66 with a pension, dividends and Social Security: joint brackets and standard deduction, but the 25,000 Social Security base and the 75,000 senior-deduction threshold.
worked:
Line numbers are those of the 2025 Form 1040, its instructions' worksheets and Schedule 1-A; the figures are the 2026 ones from the federal file.
Filing status: qualifying surviving spouse.
Taxpayer: born 1960-03-03, age 66 at the end of 2026.
Form 1040: line 3a qualified dividends 4,000; line 3b ordinary dividends 5,000; lines 4b + 5b taxable pensions and IRA distributions 60,000; line 6a Social Security benefits 30,000.
Social Security Benefits Worksheet (Form 1040 instructions, lines 6a and 6b; Publication 915 Worksheet 1):
  line 1 = 30,000; line 2 = 50% x 30,000 = 15,000
  line 3 (lines 1z, 2b, 3b, 4b, 5b, 7a, 8) = 65,000; line 4 (line 2a) = 0
  line 5 = 15,000 + 65,000 + 0 = 80,000; line 6 (Schedule 1 adjustments) = 0; line 7 = 80,000
  line 8 (base amount, qualifying surviving spouse) = 25,000
  line 9 = 80,000 - 25,000 = 55,000; line 10 = 9,000 (34,000 adjusted base amount - 25,000); line 11 = 46,000
  line 12 = smaller of 55,000 and 9,000 = 9,000; line 13 = 4,500; line 14 = smaller of 15,000 and 4,500 = 4,500
  line 15 = 85% x 46,000 = 39,100; line 16 = 4,500 + 39,100 = 43,600
  line 17 = 85% x 30,000 = 25,500; line 18 = smaller of 43,600 and 25,500 = 25,500 -> Form 1040 line 6b
Form 1040 line 9 total income = 5,000 + 60,000 + 25,500 = 90,500; line 10 adjustments 0; line 11a/11b adjusted gross income = 90,500.
Line 12e standard deduction = 32,200 basic (married filing jointly amount, used by a qualifying surviving spouse) + 1 x 1,650 additional (married or surviving spouse amount, one per box checked on line 12d for age 65 or older / blind) = 33,850.
Schedule 1-A: line 1 = line 11b 90,500; line 3 MAGI = 90,500 (no excluded income).
  Part V: line 31 = 90,500; line 32 = 75,000; line 33 = 15,500; line 34 = 6% x 15,500 = 930; line 35 = 6,000 - 930 = 5,070
  line 36a (born before January 2, 1962) = 5,070; line 37 = 5,070 -> line 38 -> Form 1040 line 13b
Line 14 = 33,850 + 5,070 = 38,920; line 15 taxable income = 90,500 - 38,920 = 51,580.
Qualified Dividends and Capital Gain Tax Worksheet (Form 1040 line 16):
  line 1 = 51,580; line 2 = 4,000; line 3 = 0 (no Schedule D; Form 1040 line 7a is 0); line 4 = 4,000; line 5 = 51,580 - 4,000 = 47,580
  line 6 = 98,900; line 7 = smaller of 51,580 and 98,900 = 51,580; line 8 = smaller of 47,580 and 51,580 = 47,580; line 9 = 4,000 taxed at 0%
  line 10 = smaller of 51,580 and 4,000 = 4,000; line 11 = 4,000; line 12 = 0
  line 13 = 613,700; line 14 = smaller of 51,580 and 613,700 = 51,580; line 15 = 47,580 + 4,000 = 51,580; line 16 = 0; line 17 = smaller of 0 and 0 = 0
  line 18 = 15% x 0 = 0; line 19 = 4,000; line 20 = 4,000 - 4,000 = 0; line 21 = 20% x 0 = 0
  line 22 (tax on line 5): Tax Rate Schedule Y-1 (married filing jointly or qualifying surviving spouse) on 47,580: 10% x 24,800 = 2,480; 12% x (47,580 - 24,800) = 2,733.60; total 5,213.60
  line 23 = 0 + 0 + 5,213.60 = 5,213.60
  line 24 (tax on line 1): Tax Rate Schedule Y-1 (married filing jointly or qualifying surviving spouse) on 51,580: 10% x 24,800 = 2,480; 12% x (51,580 - 24,800) = 3,213.60; total 5,693.60
  line 25 = smaller of 5,213.60 and 5,693.60 = 5,213.60 -> Form 1040 line 16 (regular tax)
Form 8960: lines 8 and 12 net investment income = 5,000; line 13 MAGI = 90,500; line 14 threshold = 250,000; line 15 = 90,500 - 250,000, zero or less, so 0; line 17 net investment income tax = 0.
Form 8959: no wages or self-employment income; additional Medicare tax 0.
Total tax = 5,213.60 regular + 0 net investment income tax + 0 additional Medicare tax = 5,213.60.
